tagline: A steeple and a cross at every crossroads.
intro: From St. Anthony, the village first called Padua, the route runs about 38 miles, south to Fort Recovery and then east through farm country by way of St. Henry, St. Rose and Maria Stein to Minster and McCartyville. Every small crossroads out here has a substantial church, its steeple topped with a cross.

They go back to Father Francis de Sales Brunner, who arrived from Switzerland in 1843 with the Society of the Precious Blood and founded Catholic communities across the region, and to the Swiss architect Anton DeCurtins and his descendants, who built many of the big Gothic Revival churches.

moments.title: St. Henry
moments.text: The village was platted on the feast of St. Henry in 1837, and its church was contracted at $28,300 with the parishioners to supply the extras, a bill that ended at $45,535.

moments.title: Maria Stein
moments.text: Its first settlers called the place St. Johns because every one of their men was named John, and in 1875 a priest brought holy relics from Rome to the convent here.

moments.title: Minster
moments.text: In a village named for Münster in Westphalia, St. Augustine Church of 1848 gained twin towers in 1874, with clocks on all four sides and gold crosses on top.
